title: API Triage Compendium — Unified Response Workflow (draft)
summary: Working draft: consolidated SRE triage workflow for the top API customer-facing failure modes (client timeouts, 429 rate-limits, degraded streaming, and elevated 5xx/error rates). Combines detection signals, immediate containment actions, short-term mitigations, and post-incident follow-ups.
content:
Purpose
This is a single-page operational compendium to help first responders and on-call SREs rapidly assess, contain, and mitigate common API surface degradations. It is intentionally pragmatic: prioritized actions first, investigation hooks second.

Scope
- Failure modes: client request timeouts, 429 rate-limit spikes, streaming interruptions (partial/slow frames, error-terminated streams), and elevated 5xx/error rates across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Assumes access to monitoring dashboards, logs (request+runtime), API gateway traces, and the ability to apply routing/traffic rules.

Fast triage checklist (0-5 min)
1) Verify alert context: check pager subject, affected endpoints, severity (P1/P2).
2) Look at traffic heatmap (Grafana: ops/api-traffic) — is this a sudden spike or gradual drift?
3) Open single-request trace (Jaeger/Zipkin link) for a representative failed request. Note upstream stage where time is spent (edge, gateway, runtime, model).
4) If customers report timeouts: try curl from a bastion to the endpoint with the same params; capture timing (curl -w "%{time_starttransfer}" -o /dev/null).
5) If 429s: confirm rate-limit headers in responses (x-rw-limit, Retry-After). If present, correlate to quota rules or throttle policy.
6) For streaming issues: test small streaming call with SSE/HTTP2 client, observe whether frames arrive then stall or immediate truncation.

Quick containment (5-20 min)
- Timeouts / Latency burst:
  * Enable emergency route duplication: switch a subset of traffic to a known-stable model variant (pin to low-concurrency config) or fallback region if latency SLOs are regional.
  * If sudden queue/backlog in runtime: increase worker concurrency temporarily (if autoscaler lags) or scale up instance class. Use the control plane path: /ops/scale or infra-runbook commands.
  * If source is long-tail requests (very large seqLen): apply short-lived conservative limit on max_tokens or seq_len via request inspector. Communicate via status page.
- 429 spikes:
  * Short-term: raise quotas for affected tenants that are critical (via admin portal) and apply backpressure at proxy (conn_limit per IP) to protect infrastructure.
  * Identify whether 429s are client-side (bursty clients) or system-side (exhausted tokens). If system-side, route to lower-cost tolerant variant to absorb traffic.
- Streaming degradation:
  * Toggle streaming throttle to reduce frame size: enable chunked-mode with smaller frame sizes (ops flag).
  * If proxy-level timeouts are trimming streams: extend stream keepalive/idle timeouts in gateway for 2x current for affected route.
  * If runtime reports repeated incomplete frames: enable guarded retry at proxy (resume token/offset) when supported.
- Elevated 5xx rates:
  * If 5xx is concentrated on a single host: drain and cordon it from LB, then investigate logs for OOMs, GPU driver resets, or segfaults.
  * If 5xx correlates with config rollout: rollback to previous config and open rollback ticket.

Investigation hooks (20-90 min)
Signals to capture:
- Request-level: latency P50/P95/P99 trends, error codes, upstream stage time breakdown.
- System-level: CPU/GPU utilization, memory growth, kernel OOMs, disk i/o, network drops.
- Control-plane: worker queue lengths, KV cache hit rates, connection pool saturation.
- Client behavior: burstiness, malformed payloads, or sudden change in traffic pattern (CDN cache TTL changes).
Useful queries and commands (copyable)
- Live request tail (logs): k8s logs --namespace runtime -l app=inference -c runtime --since=10m | grep "ERROR" | head -n 200
- Trace sampling: open /traces?service=inference&minDuration=300ms and filter by endpoint
- Slow-req histogram: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM api_metrics WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND time > now() - 1h
- Check worker backlog: curl -s http://runtime-metrics/queues | jq .pending

Runbook decision tree (short)
1) Is the problem global or localized?
  - Localized: drain and isolate host/pool, then continue investigation.
  - Global: look at control-plane (autoscaler, config rollout, provider outage), and execute global mitigations.
2) Is the cause traffic-driven?
  - Yes: apply adaptive throttling, short-term quota increases for critical clients, and traffic shaping for noisy tenants.
  - No: rollback recent deploys, check infra degradation, escalate to platform-eng.
3) Is streaming failing but non-stream endpoints healthy?
  - Suspect gateway/proxy timeout or HTTP2 session degradation; collect tcpdump, increase timeouts, and route new streaming sessions to healthy pool.

Escalation and communication
- When to page on-call infra: host OOMs, GPU resets, or persistent control-plane failures after 15 min of mitigation.
- When to involve product/SE: customer-impacting 429s where tenant quota changes are needed.
- Status message templates: short, factual updates every 10-15 minutes during P1. Keep customer-facing wording separate and reviewed by comms.

Post-incident items (capture within 48h)
- Root-cause hypothesis and evidence (logs, traces, config diffs).
- Action items: fixes, automation (auto-scale tuning, alert threshold adjustments), test-plan updates (synthetic traffic that covers long-tail seqLen and streaming).
- SLA/customer impact summary and suggested credits or compensatory actions (if applicable).

Operator tips and gotchas (collected from previous incidents)
- Throttles may look like 429s but are actually upstream gateway refusing due to conn limits; always confirm the x-rw-limit header first.
- Streaming stalls often present as normal 200s in logs because the connection stays open; look at bytes-sent/time and frame-level metrics.
- Rolling back a config can mask the true cause; capture a config diff before rollback.
- Curl/loadtest from bastion might not reproduce if request pattern includes client keepalive/HTTP2 multiplexing — use an HTTP2-capable test client.

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs)
- Build a small synthetic suite that tests: short burst (1k rps for 60s), long-tail sequences (10k tokens), and 100 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Add a streaming-frames-per-second panel to Grafana (currently we only show connections and bytes).
- Implement auto-rollback alarm if 5xx > 3% for 10m after a rollout.

Appendix: quick commands & links
- Grafana dashboards: ops/api-traffic, ops/api-errors, ops/streaming-monitor
- Trace UX: Jaeger service=inference
- Admin console: https://admin.redwood.internal/quotas
- Emergency scale: https://infra.redwood.internal/ops/scale (requires captain role)

Notes to self
- Keep this compendium short and pragmatic. Expand each section into separate playbooks (timeouts, 429s, streaming, rollouts) later. Capture any new mitigation discovered in the incident timeline.

End of draft.
